headline: High: Prefect can ingest ComfyUI outputs and broad egress creates a default data-leak and cascading-action pathway; prompt injection and capability conflict are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP/shared-channel surface, while Prefect is an orchestrator that can consume workflow metadata. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so the pathway is only plausible if outputs are manually copied or wired into a shared workspace. That makes the risk low, not none, because interaction is possible but not default.
conditions: IF Prefect is configured to read ComfyUI-generated text or metadata as task instructions
IF a shared filesystem or manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any parser that treats generated text as commands
Require human review before passing ComfyUI outputs into Prefect
Use a strict schema for any handoff payload
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches models, embeddings, and workflow artifacts, and Prefect has broad network egress. Even without a shared filesystem explicitly listed, a workflow handoff can move sensitive artifacts from ComfyUI into Prefect, which can then transmit them outward. The pair therefore has a plausible default leakage path, though the exact shared storage is not documented.
conditions: IF ComfyUI workflow artifacts or model assets are passed into Prefect tasks
IF Prefect sends those artifacts to external APIs or logs
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or proprietary assets through the handoff
Restrict Prefect egress to allowlisted endpoints
Store ComfyUI artifacts in a segregated directory
Redact workflow metadata before orchestration
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on Prefect inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, while Prefect is a data-engineering orchestrator with broad egress but no write surface shown here. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are not evidenced, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because Prefect's write behavior is not fully specified, so the safer low severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect is configured to write into the same directory ComfyUI uses for models or workflows
IF both agents are given write access to a shared mutable resource
mitigations: Separate writable directories per agent
Run Prefect with least-privilege filesystem access
Avoid shared git working trees
Serialize writes through one coordinator
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can operationalize workflow metadata, so if it consumes ComfyUI outputs as authoritative inputs, a bad generation can propagate into downstream automation. ComfyUI does not verify facts, and Prefect is designed for orchestration rather than semantic validation. The pair therefore supports a medium cascading-error pathway in default-style pipelines, though not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF Prefect uses ComfyUI outputs as inputs to downstream tasks without validation
IF downstream tasks act on those outputs automatically
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require human approval for downstream actions
Limit Prefect to read-only reporting on ComfyUI outputs
Add schema checks for every handoff
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before automation

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is open-source, offline-capable, and only touches local model/workflow assets; Prefect's documented surface here is workflow metadata plus GitHub API access. No residency, certification, or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps rather than a concrete breach pathway. The other agent is not cited beyond the pair context because no specific compliance surface is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Prefect workflow metadata
IF ComfyUI artifacts contain data subject to residency or retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of workflow metadata
Review retention settings for Prefect logs
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: add residency controls to orchestration
